findings.reason: the measure that proves the staging root is honoured cannot be produced without either naming those two config paths as granted writes (or recording their setting as coordinator work done before dispatch), so the node would stop or stray in scope.
findings.text: the host measure is written as node work but needs writes the node is not given: the staging root lives in each project's own flight config, `imas-efit/docs/state/imas-efit/flight.yaml` (which does not exist and must be created) and `nova/docs/state/nova/flight.yaml`, both outside s4's write paths ("reckon/crew/gc.py; reckon/crew/routing.py; the flight schema, for the staging root; the new test; and that fragment") and outside the reckon repository entirely, and the paragraph names no actor, so "These values are configuration, not code" is an intent note rather than a write grant; a fenced node either refuses the write and cannot run the measure, or writes unlisted cross-repo paths

findings.reason: restoring the timeout is one clause and is what keeps the measure from hanging on the node the plan expects it to run on; without it a later node has no bound to cite when the run stalls.
findings.text: the rewritten host measure drops the "under a timeout" bound the paragraph previously carried, while the walk it asks for recurses into trees now living on `/work` (`_newest_mtime` and `tree_size_bytes` follow the moved trees), so an unbounded dry run over the real store on the shared fleet node is now what the done-when asserts, and no timeout means a slow walk presents as a stuck node rather than a bounded measurement
